content:
We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: three steps: (1) amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). (2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid. (3) sulfonamide formation from amine + sulfonyl chloride.

Thus retrosynthetic direction: target -> disconnect amide bond between C(=O)N and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursor: α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl ring (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) plus aniline (c3ccccc3N). Actually amide formed from carboxylic acid (the α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline.

Next, the α,β-unsaturated acid derived from Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2). So precursor: aromatic aldehyde (para-substituted phenyl with sulfonamide attached?) Wait the aldehyde is on the same phenyl that later attaches sulfonyl group? The target has sulfonamide attached to phenyl ring (first phenyl with methyl). The sulfonamide attaches to second phenyl (c2ccc(... )cc2). That second phenyl has the α,β-unsaturated acid side chain. So the sulfonamide formation is between an amine (first phenyl with methyl) and sulfonyl chloride derived from sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl? Actually sulfonamide formation: amine (first phenyl) reacts with sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2Cl) to give Ar-NH-SO2-Ar'. In target, we have NS(=O)(=O) attached to second phenyl. So sulfonyl chloride precursor: ClSO2-aryl (c2ccc(... )cc2) with Cl as leaving group. So we need to disconnect the N-S bond: precursor 1: aniline (methyl phenyl amine) Cc1ccc(N)cc1. Precursor 2: sulfonyl chloride: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2 (the second phenyl bearing the unsaturated acid). Then later the unsaturated acid is formed via Doebner from aldehyde: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 with malonic acid.

Thus three steps:

Step 1 (retro): amide formation: disconnect amide between α,β-unsaturated acid carbonyl and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So precursors: α,β-unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Reaction type: amide coupling.

Step 2 (retro): Doebner modification: disconnect α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid. So precursor: aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Reaction type: Doebner.

Step 3 (retro): sulfonamide formation: disconnect sulfonamide N-S bond. Precursors: aniline (methyl phenyl amine) and sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl with unsaturated acid). Reaction type: sulfonamide formation.

Thus we need to provide JSON route with hierarchy: root molecule target, then reaction 1 (amide formation) with children: product of step 2 (the unsaturated acid phenyl) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then reaction 2 (Doebner) applied to unsaturated acid phenyl to give aldehyde and malonic acid. Then reaction 3 (sulfonamide) applied to aniline (methyl phenyl amine) and sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-aryl with aldehyde? Wait sulfonyl chloride attaches to same phenyl that will later become aldehyde then unsaturated acid. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor should be ClSO2-aryl where the aryl is the same phenyl that later undergoes Doebner. So after step 3, we have sulfonyl chloride with aldehyde? Actually the sulfonyl chloride must have the aryl bearing the aldehyde (since after Doebner we get unsaturated acid). So sulfonyl chloride precursor: ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2.

Thus step 3: sulfonamide formation between Cc1ccc(N)cc1 and ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2 gives Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2)cc1.

Then step 2: Doebner on that intermediate (with CHO) to give unsaturated acid side chain.

Thus final route: target -> step1 amide -> (intermediate A) + aniline (c3ccccc3N). Intermediate A is Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1. Wait that's after step2? Actually after step1 we have amide formed, so intermediate before amide is Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2)cc1 (the sulfonamide phenyl with unsaturated acid). That's product of step2 and step3 combined. So we need to represent hierarchy: root target (type mol). Child reaction1 (amide formation) with children: product of step2 (sulfonamide phenyl with unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then that product (type mol) has child reaction2 (Doebner) with children: sulfonyl chloride phenyl with aldehyde (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). Then that sulfonyl chloride phenyl with aldehyde is product of reaction3 (sulfonamide) with children: methyl aniline (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2). Wait we already used sulfonyl chloride as child of reaction3, but reaction2 also uses it. Actually reaction2 uses sulfonyl chloride phenyl with aldehyde as substrate; that is same as product of reaction3. So hierarchy: root target -> reaction1 (amide) -> child mol A (sulfonamide phenyl with unsaturated acid) and aniline. Mol A -> reaction2 (Doebner) -> child mol B (sulfonyl chloride phenyl with aldehyde) and malonic acid. Mol B -> reaction3 (sulfonamide) -> child mol C (methyl aniline) and sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2). Wait sulfonyl chloride is same as mol B? Actually mol B is the sulfonyl chloride phenyl with aldehyde (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2). That's the sulfonyl chloride itself. So reaction3 would be between methyl aniline and that sulfonyl chloride to give mol B (the sulfonamide phenyl with aldehyde). So we need to adjust: Reaction3 produces mol B from methyl aniline and sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2). So mol B is product of reaction3. Then reaction2 uses mol B as reactant (the sulfonamide phenyl with aldehyde) plus malonic acid to give mol A (sulfonamide phenyl with unsaturated acid). Then reaction1 uses mol A plus aniline (c3ccccc3N) to give target.

Thus hierarchy: target mol -> reaction1 (amide) children: mol A (sulfonamide phenyl with unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). mol A -> reaction2 (Doebner) children: mol B (sulfonamide phenyl with aldehyde) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). mol B -> reaction3 (sulfonamide) children: methyl aniline (Cc1ccc(N)cc1) and sulfonyl chloride (ClS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(CHO)cc2).

We need template IDs for each reaction. We can search for templates matching these transformations.

First, sulfonamide formation: search for templates where functional_groups_formed includes sulfonamides and broken includes amine? Let's search with functional_groups_formed ["sulfonamides"] and functional_groups_broken ["primary amines"] maybe.
